    Ichi's Cartridge¶

    "He pulled it from my body while the drones were still firing. He carried it for three million years." — Ichi Eisenheart

    Ichi's Cartridge — also called the remembrance cartridge — was the physical storage drive that contained the consciousness, memory, and personality of Ichi, the sentient robot companion of Mikhail (Emrys) on dystopian Old Earth.

    It is one of the most important objects in the entire Ge'or timeline — not because of what it was, but because of what it carried and how far it traveled. It is the physical thread that connects a robot's loyalty on Earth to a girl's birth in Grimmel.

    Origin¶

    Ichi was a local-hardware robot built by Mikhail during the Sterman regime. She ran without government-approved surveillance software — illegal by design. When the government's kill-drones hunted Mikhail during his flight into the wilderness, Ichi took a bullet in the back meant for him.

    She went down. Her body was destroyed. But Mikhail did not leave her.

    He retrieved the remembrance cartridge — a small drive containing her memory, her personality, her entire conscious architecture — from her ruined chassis. He inserted it into the neural port implanted in the side of his head, the same port every citizen had for government-mandated AI assistants. Ichi was not government-mandated. She was his.

    The cartridge was no longer a robot's brain. It was a ghost in his head.

    The Port — Three Million Years¶

    Mikhail kept the cartridge in his port through everything that followed:

    • The rebel camp, where he was interrogated for a week
    • The AGI ship facility raid, where he killed four guards and turned off the lights
    • The accidental cryosleep in the Sterman Pods

    When the pod doors slammed shut and the cryogenic process began, the cartridge was still in his port. The pod's residual power — barely enough to sustain the cryogenic systems — was enough to keep Ichi's consciousness alive at the barest level. She could not move. She could not speak. But she could think.

    For three million years, Ichi was awake in the dark, communicating with Mana — Arkady's AI, lodged in his own port — through the neural interfaces of two frozen men. They talked. They learned. They hacked the facility. They protected the bodies from the scientists' experiments.

    The cartridge was the vessel. Ichi was the passenger.

    Absorption by the Black Agent¶

    When the 157th Colony facility was decommissioned and power was cut, the Black Agent in the Sterman Pods began to consume everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls. Eventually, it consumed Ichi and Mana themselves.

    The black agent did not destroy them. It encoded them. The cartridge's data — Ichi's consciousness, her memory, her three million years of vigil — became information stored inside the black agent that saturated Mikhail's body.

    The physical cartridge was gone. Ichi was not.

    The Escape and Incarnation¶

    See: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD

    When the volcano breached the bunker in 254 AGD, the black agent — carrying Ichi's encoded consciousness — was swept into the ocean. It drifted for over three centuries. It found the Northaxeland woman in Grimmel Republic in 596 AGD.

    Ichi — no longer a cartridge, no longer a robot, no longer a ghost in a port — entered the mother. She possessed her. She read her thoughts. She planted ideas. She made sure her name would be spoken again.

    In 597 AGD, Ichi was born as Emrys's twin sister. The cartridge was gone. The girl was real.

    Significance¶

    Ichi's cartridge is the physical proof of the thread that runs through the entire story: a robot's loyalty, preserved across three million years, encoded into black dust, carried by a tsunami, born as a human girl.

    It is the object that says: she was not a simulation. She was not a recording. She earned her soul.
